title: Effort without Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2608.03719v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Advice can determine not only how past evidence is interpreted but whether new evidence will be produced. I study a sequence of decision makers who observe public success or failure but not one another's effort, and who pass costless causal assessments to their successors. Because a sender values success while underweighting her successor's effort cost, she has a reason to recommend more demanding actions. This motive can make encouragement uninformative. After an ambiguous failure, every equilibrium may induce inactivity, so experimentation and learning stop. When maximal effort makes outcomes insensitive to the underlying technology, the same force produces the opposite-looking trap: everyone works hard, but nobody tests whether less would suffice. translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.03719v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：建议不仅能决定过去证据如何被解释，还会影响是否会产生新证据。我研究了一系列决策者，他们观察公开的成功或失败，但无法观察到彼此的努力，并将无成本的因果评估传递给后继者。由于发送者重视成功而低估后继者的努力成本，她有理由推荐更具挑战性的行动。这种动机可能使鼓励失去信息性。在模糊失败后，每个均衡都可能诱导不作为，因此实验和学习停止。当最大努力使结果对底层技术不敏感时，同样的力量会产生相反的陷阱：每个人都努力工作，但没有人测试较少努力是否足够。崩溃在动机偏差上是单调的，而适度动机则保留了因果分歧和识别性实验。在阈值应用中，更强的动机提高...
tldr: 本文揭示了建议动机中的偏差如何导致实验和学习停止，并形成“无证据的努力”或“不作为”的双重陷阱，且崩溃随动机偏差单调增加。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals how motivational bias in advice can halt experimentation and learning, leading to twin traps of "effort without evidence" or inaction, with collapse monotonically increasing in motivational bias.
